overview: Single-site diagnostic accuracy study nested in the nurse residency program: the month-3 Transition Check (index test, cut-off 30 or below fixed in advance) is compared with separation from the hospital within 12 months of hire (reference standard) for the four intakes from October 2026 to October 2027.
population: All new graduate registered nurses in the four intakes who attend the month-3 seminar and give verbal consent; residents who leave before month 3 are counted in the flow diagram but cannot be tested.
exposure: Index test: the 15-item Transition Check (0 to 60 points), completed on paper at the month-3 seminar and scored by the residency coordinator; positive at 30 or below. Reference standard: a separation date within 365 days of hire in human resources records; transfers between units or sites of the hospital count as staying.
procedures: The coordinator enters scores into a locked study file keyed by study number. Twelve months after each resident's hire date, the human resources analyst named in HR-DR-2026-12 returns hire and separation dates by study number without access to the scores. The residency office keeps the only link between names and study numbers. Seminar timing (month 3 plus or minus two weeks) is recorded for every resident.

outcomes.name: Sensitivity and specificity at the pre-specified cut-off
outcomes.measure: Proportion of residents who separate within 12 months with a score of 30 or below, and proportion of residents who stay with a score above 30
outcomes.timing: Index test at month 3; reference standard at 12 months after hire
outcomes.why: Decides whether the score can target the booster without missing leavers or flagging too many stayers.

outcomes.name: Area under the ROC curve
outcomes.measure: Discrimination of the continuous score for separation within 12 months
outcomes.why: Shows whether another cut-off could be worth testing later.

outcomes.name: Predictive values at the local separation rate
outcomes.measure: Positive and negative predictive values at the observed rate and at 19 and 26 percent
outcomes.why: Tells the educators how many flagged residents would actually leave (claim c3).

outcomes.name: Completion of the check at the month-3 seminar
outcomes.measure: Proportion of residents in each intake with a complete Transition Check
outcomes.why: Incomplete checks would bias the accuracy estimate.

outcomes.name: Residents who feel monitored by the check
outcomes.measure: Agreement with one item at the month-6 seminar: I worry the Transition Check could be used to judge my performance
outcomes.why: The check only helps if residents answer it honestly.

feasibility: About 280 residents over four intakes; the check already takes 10 minutes of seminar time; the human resources extract is one query per intake; no extra funding is needed.
biasMitigation: Cut-off of 30 or below fixed before the first score is linked to separation data
Reference standard ascertained by an analyst without access to scores
Every tested resident receives the reference standard (no partial verification)
Transfers between units defined as staying before analysis

biasFlags.label: Incorporation or review bias
biasFlags.note: Separation dates are recorded by human resources independently of the score.

biasFlags.label: Spectrum of residents tested
biasFlags.note: Early leavers before month 3 are not tested; they are reported separately.

biasFlags.label: Timing of the index test
biasFlags.note: Seminars held later lower sensitivity elsewhere; timing is recorded for every resident.

flags: One index test, one cut-off, one reference standard; subgroup results descriptive only
parsimony.simplestPath: One score, one cut-off, one date-based reference standard, four intakes.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond the STARD 2015 accuracy framework; the transition construct is taken from the scale's own validation.
summary: Accuracy study over four intakes with one primary accuracy outcome, two secondary, one process and one balancing measure.
